title: Benchmark lab profiles, driver snapshot, and repro scaffold
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We see recurring flakiness in tokens/sec and p95 latency comparisons between runs that appear to be caused by subtle driver/CUDA differences and non-deterministic runner envs. Engineers spend 1-2 days repro-ing a slow run to find the environment mismatch (driver or pinned image), then re-run the harness. This slows regression triage and weakens our automated gates.

Goal:
Establish a reproducible, auditable benchmark lab profile and snapshot mechanism that pins driver/CUDA/runtime artifacts (container images, kernel module versions, runner config). Provide a lightweight repro scaffold that lets engineers reproduce a failing tokens/sec/p95 regression locally or in an isolated CI sandbox within 1 hour. Integrate a CI validator that fails builds when a benchmark regression is caused by unpinned environment drift rather than model/runtime code changes.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Define canonical lab profiles for our common GPU families (A10G, A100, H100) with explicit driver and CUDA package versions.
- Implement an artifact snapshot format (human readable YAML in repo + machine-checksum) for pinned images and driver binaries.
- Add an isolated "runner-lab" sandbox config that spins runners with pinned images and a KV-cache warmup protocol.
- Create local repro scaffold scripts and a lightweight harness that replays a failing workload trace against the snapshot.
- Ship a CI job (driver-snapshot-validator) that verifies snapshots are used in nightly regression runs and surfaces environment-drift as a distinct failure class.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Lab profiles for A10G, A100, H100 committed as YAML under /benchmarks/lab-profiles/*.yml.
2) Snapshot tool (benchctl snapshot --create|--verify) implemented and documented.
3) Repro scaffold can take a failing trace id and reproduce within <60 minutes in an isolated runner.
4) CI job driver-snapshot-validator added to nightly regressions; CI fails with clear error when environment drift detected.
5) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with example troubleshooting flow.
plan_steps: Inventory current CI and lab images + driver versions (collect from last 90 days of benchmark runs)
Define canonical profiles and pin lists for each GPU family
Design snapshot file format and checksumming scheme
Create runner-lab Terraform/Kubernetes manifests to launch pinned runners in isolated VPC
Build repro scaffold script that replays workload traces and collects tokens/sec and p95 stats
Add CI job and gating logic to nightly benchmark pipeline
Author documentation and runbook; run two end-to-end smoke tests and record results
rollout_strategy: Start with a single stable lab profile (A100) behind a feature-flagged CI validator for two weeks. If stable, expand to A10G and H100. Enable enforcement (fail-on-drift) only after 2 successful release cycles.
notes: Trade-offs: pinning drivers reduces variability but increases maintenance when we intentionally update kernels/drivers. We'll add a scheduled 'driver-update' cadence and a presubmit smoke bucket to validate upgrades.
Alternative considered: container-only pinning. Rejected because kernel/driver ABI mismatches were the root cause in multiple past incidents.
Security: snapshots reference checksums for signed driver packages; OSS license review required for some vendor binaries.
